key_insight: External strain can strongly tune electron and hole g-factors in bulk CsPbX3, even driving them through zero, while nanocrystals are much less strain-sensitive because of quantum confinement.
engineering_relevance: Strain engineering offers a practical route to control spin and magneto-optical behavior in lead-halide perovskites for spintronic and quantum-device design.
method: Built an 18-band k·p model for cubic CsPbX3.
Fit model parameters to DFT target band structures.
Computed g-factors with linear response theory and extended the analysis to real-space nanocrystal calculations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretically obtained bulk and nanocrystal g-factors and their strain dependence, with bulk values showing wide tunability and zero-crossing in some cases.
watch_item: Results are theoretical and focused on the reference cubic phase, so experimental validation and phase/defect effects may alter the predicted strain response.
paper_title: Strain tunability of electron and hole g-factors in CsPb$X_3$: bulk and nanocrystals
